visual_thesis: An assistant infers motives through a subjective retelling; constructed hidden motives make evaluation possible, not real-world certainty.
mechanism_metaphor: A porcelain relief whose main mass is an asymmetric branching fork. At upper center an Event record is refracted through a single tilted Subjective retelling prism; its two facets are marked Observed facts and User framing. A single downward arrow exits the retelling object into a lower open Competing motives cradle containing distinct alternative forms, neither marked correct. An Ask for details small side branch returns a question-shaped cavity without an arrowhead or question glyph, showing the source-recommended clarification option without asserting improvement. Off to the left a separate sealed Hidden motive capsule aligns with Evaluation only through a thin nondirectional comparison brace; it has no data path into the assistant. The lower-right detached scope note reads Synthetic interactions. No people, speech-bubble pseudo-text, guaranteed diagnosis, false certainty or extra motive examples. The two internal visible distinctions are facts versus framing, and candidate inference versus constructed evaluation ground truth.
